page: OVHcloud b3-256 is a general-purpose cloud instance provisioned via KVM virtualization. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running on the AMD EPYC processor family at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. For local I/O operations, the configuration includes 400 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage, and networking is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps. No graphical processing units (GPUs) are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate high multi-threaded computational and memory capabilities. The instance scored 194,618.39 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 93,194.81 on the PassMark CPU test, both registering in the top 10% tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 787.61 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations achieved 131.64 million operations per second, also placing in the top 10%. Memory throughput is robust, showing 236.54 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB read blocks. Conversely, single-threaded execution is moderate, with Geekbench single-core at 1,903.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 29.14 GB/sec, falling into the middle 50% category.

The 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation eliminates hyper-threading contention, resulting in consistent multi-core execution and high parallel efficiency. While single-thread clock performance is conservative at 2.3 GHz, the density of 64 dedicated AMD EPYC cores alongside 256 GB RAM makes it cost-efficient for parallelized enterprise workloads. This architecture is well-suited for distributed database clusters, Clang build farms, in-memory caching platforms, and data-intensive ETL processing pipelines.
description: OVHcloud b3-256 is a general-purpose virtual server built on KVM, featuring 64 dedicated physical cores from the AMD EPYC family clocked at 2.3 GHz without hyper-threading. The system pairs these cores with 256.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio, 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 16 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate exceptional parallel computing efficiency, with top-tier multi-core metrics including a stress-ng score of 194,618.39, a PassMark CPU score of 93,194.81, and over 131 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics fall into the average range due to moderate clock frequencies. Lacking GPUs, the b3-256 is designed for high-density compute tasks requiring strong multi-threading, such as large database deployments, concurrent compilation, in-memory caches, and enterprise ETL workloads.
